semantics identical (verified per site, `getUsersByRole` is now strictly narrower on unknown role strings). **Transaction scope**: `NormMappingService.suggestAndApplyMappings` no longer holds one transaction across its whole loop of multi-second OpenRouter calls — the AI phase runs untransacted and each requirement's mappings are applied in their own short transaction via a new `applyHighConfidenceSuggestions` reached through a self-`Provider` (the repo's standard AOP idiom); per-requirement failure isolation unchanged, entity re-loaded inside the transaction so nothing detached is saved. **Deadlock retry**: `CrowdStrikeVulnerabilityImportService`'s private `isDeadlockException`/`withDeadlockRetry` copy is deleted in favor of the shared `DeadlockRetry` (which had been lifted from it); the READ-COMMITTED rationale comment is preserved at the class, and the duplicated unit test dropped in favor of `DeadlockRetryTest`. **Workgroup tree**: new `GET /api/workgroups/tree` (`IS_AUTHENTICATED`, exactly the `/root`+`/children` visibility model via `accessibleWorkgroupIdsOrNull`) returns the caller's whole visible set flat with parent links; `MoveWorkgroupModal` now makes that one request instead of a serial recursive children-walk (one request per workgroup node). **Frontend**: `HomeStatisticsDashboard` runs its up-to-9 card fetches concurrently (latency = slowest, not sum) while keeping the deliberate per-card try/catch degradation; `McpDashboard`'s 30s poll no longer survives unmount (cleanup closed over a state variable that was still null at effect creation); `AssetManagement` memoizes its filtered list (previously recomputed 5× per render) and dropdown option sets; dead `utils/api-config.ts` (261 lines, zero importers) deleted; `VulnerabilityExceptionService`'s five copies of CVE-list parsing collapsed into `parseCveList`. **Removed**: `VulnerabilityService.getCurrentVulnerabilities` (legacy, `Pageable.UNPAGED` fetch-all-then-filter, zero production callers — everything uses `getCurrentVulnerabilitiesOptimized`/`getCurrentVulnerabilitiesByStatusSql`). Verification: frontend `npm ci && npm run build` clean + 257/0 unit tests; `owasp-check` 0 BLOCK (3 REVIEW decided in the PR); humanizer 0 BLOCK; `/security-review` no findings. **Backend Gradle build, backend startup and the two E2E gates could not run in the authoring environment (no Gradle distribution or dependency mirror reachable, no MariaDB, no pass-cli) — run `./gradlew build`, `./scripts/startbackenddev.sh`, `/e2ejs` and `/e2evulnexception` before merge.** Deferred by design, per the review's sequencing: email-out-of-transaction migration, hydration audit (needs `/e2ejs` per page), and all Phase-3 structural de-duplication.
7:- **AWS account display names link accounts to workgroups (2026-08-25)** — an AWS account mapping file already names the team that owns each account (`display_name` in the Cloud Custodian export, a `display_name` column in the CSV exports), and that name was being thrown away at the CLI boundary: `UserMappingCliService.parseFromJson` flattened each account to `{email, awsAccountId}` and the backend's `CSVUserMappingParser` treated the column as an ignorable extra. The rule now implemented in one place — `WorkgroupAccountLinkService` — is that an account whose display name is `DevOps-x` belongs to the workgroup **`aws-DevOps-x`**: matched **exactly** on `"aws-" + display_name`, case-insensitively via `WorkgroupRepository.findByNameIgnoreCase`, and **created** (root level, `createdBy` = the acting ADMIN) when it does not exist. Suffixed variants such as `aws-DevOps-x-rolegreen` are deliberately not matched — a fuzzy rule here would hand an unrelated workgroup's members access to an account's assets, since a link is unified-asset-access **rule #9** (`WorkgroupAwsAccount`), not bookkeeping. Reuse rather than reimplementation: creation goes through `WorkgroupService.createWorkgroup` and assignment through `WorkgroupAwsAccountService.add`, whose `actorId` became nullable (`createdBy` is already nullable since V206's ON DELETE SET NULL) so the automated path can record "no interactive actor" instead of inventing one. Two entry points, both ADMIN-only. **During an import**: `BulkUserMappingEntry` gained `displayName`, carried by CLI `manage-user-mappings import` (JSON and the optional CSV `display_name` column), REST `POST /api/user-mappings/bulk`, MCP `import_user_mappings` and REST `POST /api/import/upload-user-mappings-csv`; linking runs in `UserMappingBulkImportService.execute` **after** the mappings commit, the same ordering rule the notification and onboarding side effects already follow, and is wrapped so a linking failure is reported rather than costing an import that already persisted. **On demand**: the new correction path re-links from what is already stored, with no file involved — CLI `manage-user-mappings link-workgroups [--dry-run]`, REST `POST /api/user-mappings/link-workgroup-accounts`, MCP `link_workgroup_aws_accounts`. That is what makes the display name worth persisting: new `user_mapping.aws_account_name` (**V260**, nullable, not backfilled, indexed) is deliberately **not** part of `uk_user_mapping_composite`, because the name describes the account rather than the identity of the mapping — so a rename updates the row instead of forking a second one, and both import paths refresh the name on rows they skip as duplicates (without that, the correction path would be blind to every account whose mappings already existed). Edge cases are result rows, never exceptions, so one bad account cannot abort a 10,000-account import: a display name that cannot legally be a workgroup name (`Workgroup.name` allows letters, digits, spaces and hyphens, ≤100 chars including the prefix — so `Data_Platform.01` is refused) is an **error with nothing created**; an account already assigned is `alreadyLinked`, an idempotent no-op that never drives a non-zero exit status; a lost race on workgroup creation re-reads and links to the winner's row, and a lost race on assignment (`DuplicateAccountException`) also reads as `alreadyLinked`, the unique index being the arbiter; duplicate pairs are collapsed before any DB work; names over 255 characters are dropped rather than truncated (a truncated name resolves to a *different* workgroup) and the drop is reported in `errors[]`. When one account carries several names, the correction path uses the most recently updated mapping's — and deliberately leaves the assignment made under the old name in place, because removing one revokes a workgroup's access and a correction run must not do that unasked. Bounded at both ends (§A04): the stored-name scan is paged at the query (`findAwsAccountDisplayNames(Pageable)`, grouped so one account owned by 40 people is one row), `MAX_PAIRS` 20,000 per run and `links[]` capped at 500 with exact counters, and every cap sets `truncated` and logs — never a silent one. §A09: `CREATE_WORKGROUP_FOR_AWS_ACCOUNT` and `LINK_WORKGROUP_ACCOUNT` audit lines carry actor, target and outcome, and every display name reaching a log or an error message goes through `UserMappingService.sanitizeForMessage` (log forging). Fixed while registering the new tool: `list_/add_/remove_workgroup_aws_account` and the three `workgroup_ad_domain` tools were in `McpToolPermissions.LISTING` but **absent from `.CALLING`**, so `tools/call` denied them unconditionally — visible in `tools/list` yet uncallable, the same fail-closed shape as the earlier `add_requirement` and `export_requirements` gaps; a new test pins all seven in both tables and pins `link_workgroup_aws_accounts` to the same permission as `add_workgroup_aws_account`, since the effect is the same. Files with no display name link nothing and report nothing, so every existing Excel and plain-CSV import is byte-identical. Tests: `WorkgroupAccountLinkServiceTest` (19 cases covering the matrix above), `CSVUserMappingParserDisplayNameTest`, `UserMappingCliServiceDisplayNameTest` (including a CSV *without* the column, since commons-csv throws on `get()` for an unknown header), `LinkWorkgroupAwsAccountsToolTest`, plus new cases in `UserMappingBulkImportServiceTest`, `ImportUserMappingsToolTest` and `McpToolPermissionsTest`. Samples: `testdata/user-mappings/accounts-with-display-name.json` and `mappings-with-display-name.csv`, both covering match / create / shared-name / illegal-name in one file. `docs/AWS_ACCOUNT_WORKGROUP_LINKING.md`.
9:- **Full `excepted` recompute chunked to stop multi-minute lock holds (2026-08-24)** — `VulnerabilityRepository.recomputeExceptedAll()` was a single `UPDATE vulnerability v JOIN asset a … SET v.excepted = CASE WHEN EXISTS(…)` **with no WHERE clause**. It took exclusive row locks on every `vulnerability` row (~1.8M in production) and, through its correlated subquery, read locks on `vulnerability_exception` — holding both for the entire 53–180s transaction. Every concurrent writer to either table then blocked until lock-wait-timeout: bulk exception delete/import, CrowdStrike imports, per-asset recomputes. `DeadlockRetry` absorbed the failure, which is exactly why it stayed hidden — but the *other* operation still paid the full timeout first, observed as ~40s per `delete_all_vulnerability_exceptions` in both E2E runs, contending with "Async full excepted recompute complete: 1824736 rows in 53481 ms". Fix: `AsyncExceptionRecompute.recomputeAllChunked` drives the recompute as bounded **keyset** chunks (`CHUNK_SIZE` 10,000) through the new `recomputeExceptedForIdRange(afterId, throughId)`, each in its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction with per-chunk `DeadlockRetry`. Lock hold per transaction drops from minutes to milliseconds, so competing writers interleave between chunks instead of queueing behind one lock set; a chunk that loses a race replays only its own id range instead of the whole statement. **Keyset, not fixed-width id stepping** — the CrowdStrike import is delete-then-insert per asset, so ids are sparse and `MAX(id)` runs far ahead of the row count, which would make blind stepping spend most iterations on empty ranges. The daily 03:00 `recomputeAllExceptedScheduled` now delegates to the same driver (its orphaned `selfProvider` removed), so the nightly pass stops reintroducing the hold. Chunking gives up atomicity, and that is argued rather than assumed: the operation is already `@Async`, its documented contract is already eventual ("rows stay visible until it lands", failures "non-fatal; standing sweeps will retry"), a mid-statement failure already left partial state, and readers evaluate `v.excepted = 0` per row without a cross-table snapshot — so no guarantee is lost, and a failure now leaves a converged *prefix* rather than nothing. `recomputeExceptedAll()` is retained for the two integration tests that need single-step determinism on a tiny table, documented as not-for-production. Tests: `AsyncExceptionRecomputeChunkingTest` (5 cases pinning the traversal — sparse ids covered exactly once, half-open boundaries abutting without re-processing, no single range spanning the table) plus a `ExceptedFlagSqlAgreementIntegrationTest` case asserting the chunked statement assigns exactly what the atomic one does against a real database, with every flag pre-flipped so a skipped row cannot coincidentally match. Closes the `recomputeAll` lock-hold item open since the 2026-07-20 DB-pool work. OWASP: A01 reviewed — both new native queries bind parameters and take only primary-key boundaries from the preceding keyset read, on `@Async`/`@Scheduled` paths unreachable from any request.

The rule now implemented in one place — `WorkgroupAccountLinkService` — is that an account whose display name is `DevOps-x` belongs to the workgroup **`aws-DevOps-x`**: matched **exactly** on `"aws-" + display_name`, case-insensitively via `WorkgroupRepository.findByNameIgnoreCase`, and **created** (root level, `createdBy` = the acting ADMIN) when it does not exist. Suffixed variants such as `aws-DevOps-x-rolegreen` are deliberately not matched — a fuzzy rule here would hand an unrelated workgroup's members access to an account's assets, since a link is unified-asset-access **rule #9** (`WorkgroupAwsAccount`), not bookkeeping. Reuse rather than reimplementation: creation goes through `WorkgroupService.createWorkgroup` and assignment through `WorkgroupAwsAccountService.add`, whose `actorId` became nullable (`createdBy` is already nullable since V206's ON DELETE SET NULL) so the automated path can record "no interactive actor" instead of inventing one. Two entry points, both ADMIN-only. **During an import**: `BulkUserMappingEntry` gained `displayName`, carried by CLI `manage-user-mappings import` (JSON and the optional CSV `display_name` column), REST `POST /api/user-mappings/bulk`, MCP `import_user_mappings` and REST `POST /api/import/upload-user-mappings-csv`; linking runs in `UserMappingBulkImportService.execute` **after** the mappings commit, the same ordering rule the notification and onboarding side effects already follow, and is wrapped so a linking failure is reported rather than costing an import that already persisted. **On demand**: the new correction path re-links from what is already stored, with no file involved — CLI `manage-user-mappings link-workgroups [--dry-run]`, REST `POST /api/user-mappings/link-workgroup-accounts`, MCP `link_workgroup_aws_accounts`. That is what makes the display name worth persisting: new `user_mapping.aws_account_name` (**V260**, nullable, not backfilled, indexed) is deliberately **not** part of `uk_user_mapping_composite`, because the name describes the account rather than the identity of the mapping — so a rename updates the row instead of forking a second one, and both import paths refresh the name on rows they skip as duplicates (without that, the correction path would be blind to every account whose mappings already existed). Edge cases are result rows, never exceptions, so one bad account cannot abort a 10,000-account import: a display name that cannot legally be a workgroup name (`Workgroup.name` allows letters, digits, spaces and hyphens, ≤100 chars including the prefix — so `Data_Platform.01` is refused) is an **error with nothing created**; an account already assigned is `alreadyLinked`, an idempotent no-op that never drives a non-zero exit status; a lost race on workgroup creation re-reads and links to the winner's row, and a lost race on assignment (`DuplicateAccountException`) also reads as `alreadyLinked`, the unique index being the arbiter; duplicate pairs are collapsed before any DB work; names over 255 characters are dropped rather than truncated (a truncated name resolves to a *different* workgroup) and the drop is reported in `errors[]`. When one account carries several names, the correction path uses the most recently updated mapping's — and deliberately leaves the assignment made under the old name in place, because removing one revokes a workgroup's access and a correction run must not do that unasked. Bounded at both ends (§A04): the stored-name scan is paged at the query (`findAwsAccountDisplayNames(Pageable)`, grouped so one account owned by 40 people is one row), `MAX_PAIRS` 20,000 per run and `links[]` capped at 500 with exact counters, and every cap sets `truncated` and logs — never a silent one. §A09: `CREATE_WORKGROUP_FOR_AWS_ACCOUNT` and `LINK_WORKGROUP_ACCOUNT` audit lines carry actor, target and outcome, and every display name reaching a log or an error message goes through `UserMappingService.sanitizeForMessage` (log forging). Fixed while registering the new tool: `list_/add_/remove_workgroup_aws_account` and the three `workgroup_ad_domain` tools were in `McpToolPermissions.LISTING` but **absent from `.CALLING`**, so `tools/call` denied them unconditionally — visible in `tools/list` yet uncallable, the same fail-closed shape as the earlier `add_requirement` and `export_requirements` gaps; a new test pins all seven in both tables and pins `link_workgroup_aws_accounts` to the same permission as `add_workgroup_aws_account`, since the effect is the same. Files with no display name link nothing and report nothing, so every existing Excel and plain-CSV import is byte-identical. Tests: `WorkgroupAccountLinkServiceTest` (19 cases covering the matrix above), `CSVUserMappingParserDisplayNameTest`, `UserMappingCliServiceDisplayNameTest` (including a CSV *without* the column, since commons-csv throws on `get()` for an unknown header), `LinkWorkgroupAwsAccountsToolTest`, plus new cases in `UserMappingBulkImportServiceTest`, `ImportUserMappingsToolTest` and `McpToolPermissionsTest`. Samples: `testdata/user-mappings/accounts-with-display-name.json` and `mappings-with-display-name.csv`, both covering match / create / shared-name / illegal-name in one file. `docs/AWS_ACCOUNT_WORKGROUP_LINKING.md`.
9:- **Full `excepted` recompute chunked to stop multi-minute lock holds (2026-08-24)** — `VulnerabilityRepository.recomputeExceptedAll()` was a single `UPDATE vulnerability v JOIN asset a … SET v.excepted = CASE WHEN EXISTS(…)` **with no WHERE clause**. It took exclusive row locks on every `vulnerability` row (~1.8M in production) and, through its correlated subquery, read locks on `vulnerability_exception` — holding both for the entire 53–180s transaction. Every concurrent writer to either table then blocked until lock-wait-timeout: bulk exception delete/import, CrowdStrike imports, per-asset recomputes. `DeadlockRetry` absorbed the failure, which is exactly why it stayed hidden — but the *other* operation still paid the full timeout first, observed as ~40s per `delete_all_vulnerability_exceptions` in both E2E runs, contending with "Async full excepted recompute complete: 1824736 rows in 53481 ms". Fix: `AsyncExceptionRecompute.recomputeAllChunked` drives the recompute as bounded **keyset** chunks (`CHUNK_SIZE` 10,000) through the new `recomputeExceptedForIdRange(afterId, throughId)`, each in its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction with per-chunk `DeadlockRetry`. Lock hold per transaction drops from minutes to milliseconds, so competing writers interleave between chunks instead of queueing behind one lock set; a chunk that loses a race replays only its own id range instead of the whole statement. **Keyset, not fixed-width id stepping** — the CrowdStrike import is delete-then-insert per asset, so ids are sparse and `MAX(id)` runs far ahead of the row count, which would make blind stepping spend most iterations on empty ranges. The daily 03:00 `recomputeAllExceptedScheduled` now delegates to the same driver (its orphaned `selfProvider` removed), so the nightly pass stops reintroducing the hold. Chunking gives up atomicity, and that is argued rather than assumed: the operation is already `@Async`, its documented contract is already eventual ("rows stay visible until it lands", failures "non-fatal; standing sweeps will retry"), a mid-statement failure already left partial state, and readers evaluate `v.excepted = 0` per row without a cross-table snapshot — so no guarantee is lost, and a failure now leaves a converged *prefix* rather than nothing. `recomputeExceptedAll()` is retained for the two integration tests that need single-step determinism on a tiny table, documented as not-for-production. Tests: `AsyncExceptionRecomputeChunkingTest` (5 cases pinning the traversal — sparse ids covered exactly once, half-open boundaries abutting without re-processing, no single range spanning the table) plus a `ExceptedFlagSqlAgreementIntegrationTest` case asserting the chunked statement assigns exactly what the atomic one does against a real database, with every flag pre-flipped so a skipped row cannot coincidentally match. Closes the `recomputeAll` lock-hold item open since the 2026-07-20 DB-pool work. OWASP: A01 reviewed — both new native queries bind parameters and take only primary-key boundaries from the preceding keyset read, on `@Async`/`@Scheduled` paths unreachable from any request.

# Changelog (archived from CLAUDE.md)

The full history. Every change is written here **verbatim** when it happens; CLAUDE.md's `## Recent Changes` carries a 2–3 line summary of the three newest and nothing more. Nothing is ever summarized on the way in — this file is the greppable detail. Newest first.

## Recent Changes

Summaries of the three newest only. Every entry is written **verbatim** to `docs/CHANGELOG.md` when it happens — grep there for the full detail.

- **Source-review quick wins: hot-path queries, transaction scope, dashboard parallelism (2026-08-27)** — first execution pass over `docs/SOURCE_REVIEW_COMPLEXITY_SPEED.md` §6. `AssetFilterService` admin paths use a new `findAllIds()` projection and the scan path became two batch queries (no more full-table `findAll()` + in-memory filter); eight `findAll().filter{hasRole}` sites became role queries; `NormMappingService` no longer holds a transaction across its OpenRouter loop (per-requirement apply transactions via self-`Provider`); the private CrowdStrike deadlock-retry copy merged into shared `DeadlockRetry`; new `GET /api/workgroups/tree` replaces the frontend's recursive per-node walk; home dashboard fetches run concurrently, the `McpDashboard` interval leak is fixed, dead `utils/api-config.ts` and the legacy unpaged `getCurrentVulnerabilities` are deleted. item.stdout:
- **Source-review quick wins: hot-path queries, transaction scope, dashboard parallelism (2026-08-27)** — first execution pass over `docs/SOURCE_REVIEW_COMPLEXITY_SPEED.md` §6. `AssetFilterService` admin paths use a new `findAllIds()` projection and the scan path became two batch queries (no more full-table `findAll()` + in-memory filter); eight `findAll().filter{hasRole}` sites became role queries; `NormMappingService` no longer holds a transaction across its OpenRouter loop (per-requirement apply transactions via self-`Provider`); the private CrowdStrike deadlock-retry copy merged into shared `DeadlockRetry`; new `GET /api/workgroups/tree` replaces the frontend's recursive per-node walk; home dashboard fetches run concurrently, the `McpDashboard` interval leak is fixed, dead `utils/api-config.ts` and the legacy unpaged `getCurrentVulnerabilities` are deleted. Backend build/startup + E2E gates still owed before merge (authoring env had no Gradle mirror/DB/pass-cli) — detail in `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.

- **AWS account display names link accounts to workgroups (2026-08-25)** — an account whose `display_name` is `DevOps-x` now belongs to workgroup **`aws-DevOps-x`**: matched exactly (case-insensitively) on the `aws-` prefix, **created** when missing. One implementation, `WorkgroupAccountLinkService`, reached from the import (CLI/REST/MCP `displayName`, after the mappings commit) and from a correction path that re-links from stored names with no file — CLI `manage-user-mappings link-workgroups`, `POST /api/user-mappings/link-workgroup-accounts`, MCP `link_workgroup_aws_accounts`. The name is persisted as `user_mapping.aws_account_name` (V260) and deliberately kept **out** of the unique key. A display name that cannot be a workgroup name is an error row, never a forced creation; already-linked accounts are idempotent no-ops. Also fixed: six workgroup MCP tools were in `LISTING` but not `.CALLING` (listed yet uncallable). `docs/AWS_ACCOUNT_WORKGROUP_LINKING.md`.

- **Full `excepted` recompute chunked to stop multi-minute lock holds (2026-08-24)** — `recomputeExceptedAll()` was one `UPDATE` with **no WHERE**, locking every `vulnerability` row (~1.8M) plus `vulnerability_exception` for 53-180s, so every concurrent writer (bulk exception delete/import, CrowdStrike import, per-asset recompute) queued behind it. `AsyncExceptionRecompute.recomputeAllChunked` now drives bounded **keyset** chunks (`CHUNK_SIZE` 10,000) through `recomputeExceptedForIdRange`, each its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction with per-chunk `DeadlockRetry`. Atomicity is deliberately given up (the path is already `@Async` and eventual); a failure now leaves a converged prefix. `recomputeExceptedAll()` is retained for integration tests only. `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.

The full history. Every change is written here **verbatim** when it happens; CLAUDE.md's `## Recent Changes` carries a 2–3 line summary of the three newest and nothing more. Nothing is ever summarized on the way in — this file is the greppable detail. Newest first.

- **Source-review quick wins: hot-path queries, transaction scope, dashboard parallelism (2026-08-27)** — first execution pass over `docs/SOURCE_REVIEW_COMPLEXITY_SPEED.md` §6 (Phases 1–2). **Access-path queries**: the ADMIN/SECCHAMPION short-circuits in `AssetFilterService` now use a new `AssetRepository.findAllIds()` projection instead of materializing the whole asset table twice per request just to extract ids; the non-admin scan path replaced `scanRepository.findAll()` + in-memory uploader filtering (and a per-workgroup user-query loop) with two batch queries, `UserRepository.findByWorkgroupsIdInOrderByUsernameAsc` and `ScanRepository.findByUploadedByInOrderByScanDateDesc` — same predicate, same result set, no full-table scan.
